says: The vi lock, a pair of oxlint's own rules, does not refuse a call chained onto an aliased vi, such as v.spyOn(o, "m").mockImplementation(...) after import { vi as v } from "vitest", which 0555 bans.
proof: On oxlint 1.90.0 (the lockfile's), with the lock on, in a test file of a locked folder: v.spyOn(console, "log") fires vitest(no-restricted-vi-methods), and v.spyOn(console, "warn").mockImplementation(() => undefined) fires nothing. vitest/no-restricted-vi-methods misses chained calls (oxc#29656), and eslint/no-restricted-properties names the object vi, so it never sees v. VI_LOCK in oxlint-plugins/builtin-plants.ts holds the line as a documented pass (false, false), run by the V1 scenario in oxlint-plugins/plants.test.ts.
cost: A test can still spy through an aliased vi with a chained call, with no lint failure, until oxc fixes the chain or a trusted rule that follows the alias is found.
